meta_title: VHS Near Me — find a place to digitize tapes and photos
meta_description: Independent directory of local shops and mail-in labs that convert VHS, camcorder tapes, film, photos, slides, and negatives to digital files.
title: Find a place to get VHS, film, and photos digitized.
lede: VHS Near Me lists local transfer shops and compares mail-in labs. The first city page covers Dallas–Fort Worth, including Flower Mound, Lewisville, and Denton. Every price is copied from the business’s own site, or the listing says to call.
what: People still have closets of VHS, VHS-C, Hi8, Video8, MiniDV, 8mm and Super 8 film, photo prints, slides, and negatives. The players and scanners are disappearing faster than the media. This site is a directory of places that will transfer that material to files you can actually open.

It has two halves. City pages are for drop-off and local pickup, where the tapes stay in town. The mail-in page compares companies that send a box or a label and do the work at their own lab. Use a city page when you do not want to ship the only copy. Use mail-in when you have a large, ordinary collection and you have read the current price.

choose.title: Sort the formats first
choose.text: A low VHS price does not mean the shop scans slides or transfers MiniDV. Read the format guides, then match the stack you actually have.

choose.title: Decide if the originals can travel
choose.text: Local drop-off keeps a one-of-a-kind tape in the same metro area. Mail-in is a fair choice for a large box of ordinary tapes and prints. Photograph the labels and keep your own inventory before anything ships.

choose.title: Read the unit, not just the dollar sign
choose.text: Per tape, per minute, per foot of film, and per photo are different deals. A prepaid “10 item” kit can cost more than a per-tape shop once you add the empty-box shipping, a USB drive, and discs.

choose.title: Ask four questions before you pay
choose.text: What happens to a moldy or broken tape? Do the originals come back? Is the result an MP4 you can copy, or only a DVD? What is the turnaround this month, not the one printed on an old page?

choose.title: Skip copyrighted movies
choose.text: Labs in this directory transfer footage and photos you own. They are not a way to copy store-bought movies or recorded television. Shops that say they will do that are a reason to walk away.

formats_intro: Short practical notes on what each format is, what a finished transfer should include, and what to ask. The guides do not rank shops.
cities_intro: Each city page is generated from a file in data/cities. Dallas–Fort Worth is the first one. New cities show up here, on the cities index, and in the sitemap after a rebuild.
mail_intro: National services publish a price and a turnaround you can compare without calling. The figures below are the short version. The comparison page has the units, the add-ons, and the source link for each one.
